en: Having received the empowerment through the eighteen mudrās from the master, and once the authorization has been granted, one shall achieve accomplishment before long.
Only when a disciple possesses these characteristics may the transmission be bestowed; this is indeed the wish-fulfilling jewel, capable of accomplishing all things.
Regarding the site for the practice:
as the sutras describe, it should be in mountain valleys, by flowing streams, in pure *āraṇyakas*, or in pleasant ravines—places free from all calamities, fears, and hardships.

Providing offerings according to one's capacity, the practitioner faces their own direction and prostrates to the principal deity; next, they prostrate to the Buddhas of the other directions, performing the respectful salutation by placing the five limbs upon the ground as taught. Having knelt with both knees on the ground, they join their palms with hollowed palms and remain thus, sincerely confessing all transgressions of the three karmas:
"From past lives until now, wandering through birth and death, I now, before the Great Holy Honored One, confess with all my heart."
Just as the Buddhas of the past have performed confession, so do I now; may you graciously bestow the power of your empowerment, so that all sentient beings may be completely purified.
By virtue of this great vow, may both myself and others attain stainlessness.

The mantra is: *Oṃ sarvabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ sarvabhāvaśuddho ’haṃ*. Next, before the deity, sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) or the half-lotus posture (*ardhaparyaṅka*), and arouse the mind of great compassion:
"I practice this dharma for the sake of all sentient beings, so that they may swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment."

First, grind various fragrances and apply them to the hands. Then, form the Samaya-dhāraṇī-mudrā of the Buddha Family: join the two hands with palms hollowed together, extend the two index fingers, and bend them to rest against the upper joints of the two middle fingers; bend the two thumbs to rest against the lower joints of the two index fingers. Once the mudrā is formed, place it at the heart and visualize the Tathāgata’s thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs as clearly as if they were before one's eyes. Recite the mantra seven times with a sincere mind.

The mantra is: *Oṃ tathāgatodbhavāya svāhā*. By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one immediately awakens all Tathāgatas, who shall all protect, mindfully regard, and empower the practitioner. Through their illumination and touch with light, all karmic obstacles and hindrances are completely extinguished; one’s lifespan becomes long, and merit and wisdom increase. The holy assembly of the Buddha Family will provide protection and rejoice; in birth after birth, one will be free from all evil realms and, through miraculous birth within a lotus, swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Next is the Samaya of the Lotus Family: With both hands joined in the hollowed *añjali* mudrā, extend the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers, bending them into the shape of a lotus flower and placing it at the heart. Visualize Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva endowed with all the marks and signs of perfection, and recite the mantra seven times, dispersing the mudrā over the right side of the crown.
The mantra is:

"Oṃ padmanābha svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one awakens the assembly of holy beings of the Lotus Family, such as Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; they all joyfully bestow their empowerment and protective mindfulness. The light of all Bodhisattvas shines upon and touches [the practitioner], whereby all karmic obstructions are completely extinguished, and all Bodhisattvas constantly act as virtuous friends.

Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family: Turn the palm of the left hand outward; place the back of the right palm upon the back of the left hand; interlace the thumbs and little fingers of both hands like the shape of a vajra; place it at the heart while visualizing the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi; recite the mantra seven times and release the mudrā over the crown of the head toward the left.
The mantra is:

“Oṃ vajranāvaya svāhā. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one immediately awakens all the holy beings of the Vajra family, who provide empowerment and protection; all karmic obstacles and transgressions are completely extinguished, no illness or suffering shall afflict the body, and one shall attain a body as firm and solid as a vajra.

Next, perform the binding of the *samaya* for protecting the body: Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward, the right hand pressing over the left. Extend the middle fingers of both hands and bend the index fingers into the shape of hooks, ensuring they do not touch the backs of the middle fingers. Press the two thumbs together against the ring fingers, and it is thus accomplished.

Seal the five places of the body—namely, the forehead, then the right shoulder, then the left shoulder, then the heart, then the throat—and scatter [the mudrā] over the crown of the head, reciting the mantra once for each.

The mantra is: *Oṃ vajrāṅgini pratinipātaya svāhā*. By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra with empowerment, one immediately becomes clad in the adamantine armor (*vajrakavaca*). All Vināyakas and various celestial Māras who create obstacles will retreat and flee. Seeing the practitioner’s body enveloped in light and possessing sovereign majesty, they shall be entirely fearless whether dwelling in mountain forests or amidst perilous difficulties. All calamities such as water and fire, all misfortunes, and matters such as tigers, wolves, lions, swords, staves, shackles, and fetters shall be completely extinguished. Those who see them will rejoice; after the end of their lives, they shall not fall into the evil realms, but shall be reborn in the pure and wondrous lands of the Buddhas.

Next, perform the mudrā and mantra for binding the boundary of the earth (*bhūmibandha*). Insert the right ring finger into the space between the left ring finger and the little finger; insert the right middle finger into the space between the left middle finger and the index finger; do the same for the left hand. All remaining fingers should be pressed together at their tips. Visualize that the mudrā forms a flaming vajra. Place the thumbs on the ground and pull them away; recite the mantra once for each pull, up to three times, then stop. Establish the mental focus according to the desired size of the area, and the boundary of the earth will become firm and secure.
The mantra is:

*Oṃ kili kili vajra vajri bhūri bhaṇḍa bhaṇḍa hūṃ phaṭ*. By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra to empower the boundary of the ground, from here down to the limits of the waters, it becomes like a Vajrāsana; the celestial Māras and all obstructors shall not cause harm, and with little exertion, one will swiftly attain accomplishment.

Next, bind the mantra and mudrā of the Vajra Wall of the Directions and Quarters. Following the previous earth-boundary mudrā, extend the two thumbs and hold them upright so that their sides form the shape of a wall. Visualize the mudrā as having the form of a vajra. Circumambulate the body three times to mark the extent of the heart and the other points; thus, a firm vajra city is established. Even the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not transgress it, let alone other difficult-to-subdue beings; neither Vināyakas nor venomous insects with sharp fangs and claws can approach it.

The mantra is: *Oṃ sara sara vajraprakāra hūṃ phaṭ*. Next, the practitioner should visualize that within the maṇḍala, upon an eight-petaled great lotus flower, there is a lion throne. Upon the throne is a pavilion made of the seven precious jewels, draped with various necklaces, silken streamers, banners, and canopies. Rows of jeweled pillars stand in order, hanging with exquisite celestial garments and spreading clouds of incense. Various flowers rain down everywhere as music is played; there are jeweled vases and argha-offerings, divine and wondrous foods and drinks, and lamps made of mani-jewels.
Having performed this visualization, recite this verse:
"By the power of my merit, the power of the Tathāgata’s empowerment,
and the power of the Dharma-realm, I abide in universal offering."

Having spoken this verse, next, one binds the Great Ākāśagarbha Universal Offering Seal (*mudrā*): Join the two hands in *añjali*; interlace the two middle fingers with their backs facing outward; support the two index fingers against each other, curling them back like the shape of a jewel. Once the seal has been formed, recite the mantra four times.
The mantra for general offerings is:

"Oṃ gaganasamapada. By empowering through the recitation of this mantra, the visualized offering implements become truly no different from the actual ones, and all the assemblies of worthy sages and saints are able to partake of them.

Next, one should perform the mudrā of the precious chariot (*ratnaratha*). Interlace the two hands with palms facing upward, cross the index fingers so they rest against each other, and place both thumbs beneath the roots of the respective index fingers. Visualize that the precious chariot, drawn by vajra-horses, travels through the air to the World of Ultimate Bliss (*Sukhāvatī*) of the Honored One. Recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is: "Oṃ tulu tulu hūṃ.

Through the empowerment of this mantra and mudrā, the seven-jeweled chariot arrives at the land of the Honored One. Visualize that the Honored One, surrounded by a retinue of all the holy assemblies, mounts the precious chariot and dwells in the space above the ritual site.

Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the celestial chariot (*ratha*). Following the previous mudrā, bend the thumb toward the body and push the tip of the middle finger away while reciting the mantra three times.
The mantra is as follows:

*Namo siddhārthadivikānām tathāgatānām | Oṃ vairocaniye kṛṣaye svāhā.* By the empowerment of binding this mantra-mudrā, the assembly of holy ones comes from their own lands and dwells in the air above the site of practice (*maṇḍala*).

Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the Samaya of the Principal Deity to descend into the ritual arena: interlace the two hands with palms facing inward to form fists; insert the left thumb into the palm, then beckon the right thumb toward oneself.
The mantra is:

“Oṃ īṅkara oṃ alulika oṃ vajratilaka agre-agre svāhā. Through the empowerment of this mantra and mudrā, and because the deity does not transgress their original vow, they immediately arrive and assemble at the ritual site.

Next, one should expel all obstructors by forming the mudrā and reciting the mantra of the Lotus Family Vidyārāja, Avalokiteśvara Hayagrīva. Join the two palms together; bend the two index fingers and the two ring fingers so that their nails face each other within the palms; extend the two thumbs upright and apart. Rotate this mudrā three times counter-clockwise while visualizing the expulsion of all obstructors; upon seeing this mudrā, all Māras will retreat and flee. Then, rotate the mudrā three times clockwise, whereby a firm fire-element boundary is established.
The mantra is:

*Oṃ amṛtodbhava hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Next, form the Vajra-Net mudrā for the upper direction. Following the previous wall mudrā, join the two thumbs to press against the lower joints of the two index fingers; recite the mantra three times, rotate it three times clockwise above the head, and then cease.
The mantra is:
"Oṃ viśvapralocakṣa vajra-panjara hūṃ phaṭ. By means of the empowerment of this net-seal mantra, it immediately becomes a vajra-net, firm, solid, and indestructible.

Next, bind the mudrā of the secret seam for the fire enclosure (*vahnimaṇḍala*). Cover the back of the right hand with the left hand, extend the two thumbs, and recite the mantra three times. Circumambulate the body three times to the right, visualizing that the fire enclosure surrounds the vajra wall.
The mantra is:

"Oṃ asamañji hūṃ phaṭ. Next, for the offering of arghya perfumed water, perform the mantra and mudrā: holding the vessel with both hands, visualize bathing the feet of the assembly of noble ones, and recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ āgana-samaṃ samaṃ svāhā*. By offering this argha perfumed water, the practitioner’s three karmas are purified, washing away the defilements of affliction.

Next, perform the mudrā for offering the lotus seat: Join the two hands with palms hollowed together; extend the left and right ring fingers, middle fingers, and index fingers, and bend them to form the shape of a slightly blossomed lotus. Within the precious pavilion, visualize the assembly of holy ones and the principal deity each seated in their respective positions, surrounded by their retinues, appearing with perfect clarity. Recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is:
"Oṃ kamala svāhā. By forming the flower-seat mudrā and reciting this mantra, the practitioner shall attain the fulfillment of the ten stages (daśabhūmi) and shall obtain the vajra-throne.

Next, form the seal of universal offering (*samantapūjā-mudrā*): join the two hands in *añjali*, with the right hand pressing over the left, interlacing the fingers. Recite the mantra three times, while visualizing immeasurable and boundless oceans of clouds of ointment, oceans of clouds of flower garlands, oceans of clouds of burning incense, and oceans of clouds of food, drink, lamps, and so forth—all becoming pure, vast, and manifold offerings for the universal offering.
The mantra is:

*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ svāhā khaṃ udanate sphara hīṃ gaganakhe svāhā*. Regarding the eighteen mudrās, tradition states they were composed by Preceptor Kūkai (Egaku Oshō), though some say they were created by the Great Master Kōbō Daishi.
Now, according to the catalog of the Thirty Fascicles Collection (Sanjū-teshō-shō), it says:
"The Scripture of the Great Holy Joyful Deity (Daishō-kangi-ten-kyō), one fascicle, translated by Amoghavajra; at the end are eighteen sequences of neck-mantras (kei). It further states:
"Sanskrit characters for the eighteen sequences of mantras."
Reflecting on this, did the Great Master record these two versions?
Regarding the *Brief Verses on the Arising of the Eighteen Mudrās*, according to the intent of their arising:
first, the fivefold adornment of the practitioner—purifying the Buddha-lotus, [attaining] gold, and donning the armor.
Second, the two types of boundary-binding rituals: first, binding the ground; second, the vajra wall.
Third, the two ways of adorning the maṇḍala: the maṇḍala itself and universal offerings to the void.
Fourth, the three types of invitation rituals: the invitation by chariot, the escorting of the chariot, and the formal entreaty.
Fifth, the three types of the ritual for binding and protecting the Dharma: the net of fire of the vidyārāja of the respective family;
sixth, the three types of the ritual for making offerings: the general offering of argha, flowers, and seats;
the first two are specific offerings, while the latter is the exclusive offering presented solely to the principal deity.
The final offering is the general offering, presented to the primary deity and the assembly of all holy beings;
comprising six general and eighteen specific ritual procedures, these are known as the eighteen mudrās.
Regarding the generation stage (*utpattikrama*):
one who wishes to enter the gateway of the secret dhāraṇī must first refine, purify, and adorn the body;
once the body has been refined, purified, and adorned, one should likewise empower the ground of the pure realm.
Once the matters of the empowerment of the realms and stages have been cultivated, one must adorn the maṇḍala;
once the maṇḍala has been adorned, one should invite the Great Holy Honored One, the Principal Deity.
With courageous diligence, one binds the protective dharmas, binding and protecting both the internal and external so that there are no obstacles.
Thereafter, one should present offerings; without rising from one's seat, one shall accomplish *siddhi*.
